title: Hummus-y Korean Kale Namul
description: A paleo-friendly, weeknight Korean dish featuring the creamy tang of hummus, the char-grilled depth of yang, and a hint of almond extract. This mustardy namul pairs perfectly with a variety of grains, meats, or on its own as a snack.

ingredients.name: hummus
ingredients.notes: store-bought or homemade, whichever suits your taste

instructions: In a large bowl, massage the kale with your hands for 2-3 minutes to break down the fibers.
Add the hummus, ginger, garlic, and almond extract to the bowl and mix well.
Heat the sesame oil in a small skillet over medium heat.
Add the sliced yang to the skillet and cook for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the cooked yang to the bowl with the kale mixture and toss to combine.
Season with soy sauce to taste.
Transfer the namul to a serving dish and garnish with thinly sliced green onions.
Serve immediately, while the yang is still warm and fragrant.
Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
Reheat the namul in the microwave or on the stovetop before serving.
Adjust the seasoning as needed before serving.
